chapters.title: Unit 1: Problem Solving and Algorithm Designing

lessons.title: Problem Solving and Its Steps

mcqs.q: What is a problem, as defined in this lesson?
options: A task that has to be solved
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a task that has to be solved. The lesson defines a problem in exactly these words, and a finished solution or a program is the result of solving it, not the problem itself.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is given in the lesson as an example of a problem?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: baking a cake. The lesson says that 'to bake a cake' is a problem, because baking a cake is a task to be solved, and the steps for doing it form its algorithm.

mcqs.q: What is the first step of problem solving?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: identifying and analyzing the problem. The lesson states that to find a feasible solution, the first step is to identify and analyze the problem, which is also called defining the problem.

mcqs.q: The first step of problem solving, 'Define the problem', means:
options: Making a list of possible solutions
Identifying and describing the real problem
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: identifying and describing the real problem. In the four steps of problem solving, defining the problem means identifying and describing the real problem before any solutions are made.

mcqs.q: The second step of problem solving, 'Generate alternative solutions', means:
options: Making a list of possible solutions
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: making a list of possible solutions. The lesson explains the second step as making a list of possible solutions, while choosing the best one belongs to the third step.

mcqs.q: In the third step, 'Evaluate and select an alternative', we:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: choose the best solution. Evaluating and selecting an alternative means looking at the possible solutions and choosing the best one to carry forward.

mcqs.q: The fourth step, 'Implement and follow up on the solution', involves:
options: Measuring the results and seeing whether the solution worked
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: measuring the results and seeing whether the solution worked. The last step puts the chosen solution into practice and then follows up by measuring the results.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct order of the four steps of problem solving?
options: Define, Generate alternatives, Evaluate and select, Implement and follow up
Evaluate and select, Define, Generate alternatives, Implement
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the order: define the problem, generate alternative solutions, evaluate and select an alternative, and then implement and follow up. The lesson lists the four steps in exactly this sequence.

mcqs.q: To find a feasible solution to a problem, the first step is to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: identify and analyze the problem. The lesson repeats that the problem-solving process always begins with defining or identifying the problem, before solutions are generated.

mcqs.q: In the cake example of the lesson, the steps for baking the cake are called its:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: algorithm. The lesson explains that baking a cake is the problem, and the steps for doing it are its algorithm, which links this lesson to the next one on algorithms.

lessons.notes_html:
What is a problem?

A problem is a task that has to be solved. For example, "to bake a cake" is a problem — baking a cake is a task / problem to be solved, and the steps for doing it are its algorithm.

The first step of problem solving

To find a feasible solution to a problem, the first step is to identify and analyze the problem — in the problem-solving process, the first step is defining / identifying the problem.

The four steps of problem solving

  • 1. Define the problem: identifying and describing the real problem.
  • 2. Generate alternative solutions: making a list of possible solutions.
  • 3. Evaluate and select an alternative: choosing the best solution.
  • 4. Implement and follow up on the solution: measuring the results and seeing whether the solution worked.

lessons.title: Algorithms: Advantages and Writing Algorithms

mcqs.q: What is an algorithm?
options: The step by step solution of a problem in simple language
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the step by step solution of a problem in simple language. The lesson defines an algorithm this way and adds that it is a set of instructions, steps or rules for solving a problem.

mcqs.q: An algorithm is a set of:
options: Instructions, steps or rules for solving a problem
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: instructions, steps or rules for solving a problem. The lesson describes an algorithm as a set of instructions or steps or rules that are followed to solve a problem.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an advantage of developing an algorithm?
options: It gives the best possible answer every time
It removes the need for a computer
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it gives the best possible answer every time. The lesson lists this as an advantage of algorithms, along with accuracy and solving similar problems again and again.

mcqs.q: Algorithms help in work that needs:
options: Accuracy, and solving similar problems again and again
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: accuracy, and solving similar problems again and again. The lesson says an algorithm helps in work needing accuracy and in solving similar problems repeatedly.

mcqs.q: Computer programs can be built with the help of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: algorithms. The lesson clearly states that computer programs can be built with the help of algorithms, because a program follows the steps set out in the algorithm.

mcqs.q: In a good algorithm, the input and output are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: precise. The lesson says that in a good algorithm the input and output are precise and every step is clear, so the result can be trusted.

mcqs.q: Which quality belongs to a good algorithm?
options: It can be used in only one language
Every step is clear and it can be used in any programming language
It has no input or output
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: every step is clear and it can be used in any programming language. The lesson lists precise input and output, clear steps and use in any programming language as marks of a good algorithm.

mcqs.q: In the algorithm to find the greater of two numbers, which variables are declared?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: num1, num2 and greater. Step 2 of that algorithm declares the variables num1, num2 and greater, and then the two values are read and compared.

mcqs.q: In the algorithm for the area of a triangle, the formula applied is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: area = (base x height) / 2. Step 4 of the triangle algorithm applies the formula Area = (base x height) / 2 before the area is displayed.

mcqs.q: In the cake-baking algorithm, which step comes immediately after 'Preheat the oven'?
options: Put the pan in the oven
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: gather the ingredients. The lesson gives the cake steps in order: Start, preheat the oven, gather the ingredients, mix them, grease a pan, and so on until End.

lessons.notes_html:
What is an algorithm?

An algorithm is the step by step solution of a problem in simple language. It is a set of instructions / steps / rules for solving a problem.

Advantages of developing algorithms

  • An algorithm gives the best possible answer every time.
  • It helps in work needing accuracy and in solving similar problems again and again.
  • Computer programs can be built with the help of algorithms.
  • In a good algorithm the input and output are precise, every step is clear, and it can be used in any programming language.

Algorithm: find the greater of two numbers

Step 1: Start

Step 2: Declare variables num1, num2 and greater

Step 3: Read values num1 and num2

Step 4: If num1 is greater than num2 then greater = num1, else greater = num2

Step 5: Display greater

Step 6: Stop

Algorithm: area of a triangle

Step 1: Start

Step 2: Declare variables base, height and area

Step 3: Read values base and height

Step 4: Apply formula {Area = (base x height) / 2}, i.e. area = (base x height) / 2

Step 5: Display area

Step 6: Stop

Ordering the steps: baking a cake

The steps of the cake-baking algorithm in correct order: Start; Preheat the oven; Gather the ingredients; Mix together the ingredients to make the batter; Grease a pan; Pour the batter into the pan; Put the pan in the oven; Set a timer; When the timer goes off, take the pan out of the oven; End.

lessons.title: Flowcharts: Symbols, Advantages and Drawing Flowcharts

mcqs.q: A flowchart is:
options: The pictorial or graphical representation of the problem-solving process
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the pictorial or graphical representation of the problem-solving process. The lesson defines a flowchart this way and adds that it shows the logic of a program graphically.

mcqs.q: Which flowchart symbol is used for Start and Stop?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: oval. The symbol table in the lesson shows the oval for Start and Stop, while the parallelogram, rectangle and diamond have different uses.

mcqs.q: The parallelogram symbol in a flowchart is used for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Input / Output. According to the lesson's symbol table, the parallelogram is used for input and output steps in a flowchart.

mcqs.q: The rectangle symbol in a flowchart is used for:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: processing, that is, calculation steps. The lesson's symbol table assigns the rectangle to processing steps where calculations are performed.

mcqs.q: The diamond symbol in a flowchart is used for:
options: A decision, where a choice is needed
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a decision, where a choice is needed. The lesson states that the diamond is used for a decision, and in the flowchart pattern the diamond appears wherever a choice is needed.

mcqs.q: One advantage of designing a flowchart is that it:
options: Removes the need for an algorithm
Communicates the logic of a program to others and makes it easy to understand
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it communicates the logic of a program to others and makes it easy to understand. The lesson lists this as an advantage, along with being a useful program document.

mcqs.q: While coding a program, a flowchart works as a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a guide or blueprint. The lesson says flowcharts work as a guide or blueprint while coding a program, because they show the operations and their sequence visually beforehand.

mcqs.q: In the gross salary problem, the house rent allowance is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 20% of basic salary. The lesson's gross salary flowchart adds 20% house rent and 30% medical allowance to the basic salary.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, Gross Salary is equal to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 150% of Basic Salary. Basic salary plus 20% house rent plus 30% medical allowance makes 150% of the basic salary, as the lesson concludes.

mcqs.q: In the gross salary flowchart, the 'Input basic salary' step is drawn in a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: parallelogram. Input steps use the parallelogram symbol, so 'Input basic salary' and 'Display Gross Salary' are parallelograms, while the calculations are rectangles.

lessons.notes_html:
What is a flowchart?

A flowchart shows the logic of a program graphically. It is the pictorial / graphical representation of the problem-solving process.

Flowchart symbols

SymbolUsed for
OvalStart and Stop
ParallelogramInput / Output
RectangleProcessing — calculation steps
DiamondDecision — where a choice is needed

Advantages of designing flowcharts

  • Flowcharts communicate the logic of a program to others and make it easy to understand.
  • They are useful program documents with which a program can be quickly understood or its logic changed.
  • They work as a guide / blueprint while coding a program.
  • They show the operations of solving a problem and their sequence visually before writing it.

Flowchart: gross salary

Problem: calculate gross salary by adding 20% house rent and 30% medical allowances in basic salary. Flowchart: Start (oval) — Input basic salary (parallelogram) — House Rent = Basic Salary x 20 / 100 and Medical Allowance = Basic Salary x 30 / 100 (rectangle) — Gross Salary = Basic Salary + House Rent + Medical Allowance (rectangle) — Display Gross Salary (parallelogram) — Stop (oval). So Gross Salary = 150% of Basic Salary.

Drawing flowcharts for all the algorithms of this unit

The flowchart of every algorithm follows the same pattern: Start (oval) — Input (parallelogram) — calculation steps (rectangle) — Display result (parallelogram) — Stop (oval); where a choice is needed, the decision diamond is used. Making tea, sum of two numbers, average of three numbers, volume of a box, percentage, greater number, area of a triangle and gross salary — each flowchart is made by turning that algorithm's steps into these shapes; the model in the unit (the sum-and-percentage flowchart with the percent > 70 decision) is an example of it.

lessons.title: Data Structures: Array, Stack and Queue

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a non-linear data structure?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: graph. The lesson states that a graph is a non-linear data structure whose elements are not connected in sequence, while array, queue and stack are linear data structures.

mcqs.q: Every element of an array is identified by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: an index. The lesson says every element of an array is identified by an index, and indexes are consecutive numbers with which any element can be directly found and used.

mcqs.q: Traversing an array means:
options: Accessing each and every element of the array
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: accessing each and every element of the array. The lesson defines traversing an array in exactly these words, and without an index it would not be known which element is stored where.

mcqs.q: When data is pushed in a stack, it means data is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: inserted. The lesson explains that when data is pushed in a stack, data is inserted, and the new element enters from the top of the stack.

mcqs.q: In a stack, the Pop operation:
options: Adds an element at the rear
Checks if the stack is full
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it removes the top element. In the sketch of a stack in the lesson, with Push a new element enters from the top and with Pop the top element is removed.

mcqs.q: A stack is in the Overflow state when:
options: It is completely full and nothing can be added to it
An element is removed from it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: when it is completely full and nothing can be added to it. The lesson defines the overflow state of a stack in exactly this way.

mcqs.q: In a queue, the Enqueue operation makes a new element enter at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the rear end. The lesson's queue sketch shows that with Enqueue a new element enters at the rear end of the queue.

mcqs.q: In a queue, the Dequeue operation removes an element from:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the front end. According to the lesson, with Dequeue an element is removed from the front end of the queue, which is the opposite end from where elements enter.

mcqs.q: A stack works in which order?
options: LIFO / FILO - last in, first out
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: LIFO / FILO, last in, first out. The comparison table in the lesson says a stack works in LIFO order because data is added or removed only from the top.

mcqs.q: A queue works in which order?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: FIFO, first in, first out. The lesson's stack-versus-queue table states that a queue works in FIFO order, with enqueue and dequeue as its operations.

lessons.notes_html:
Linear and non-linear data structures

A graph is a non-linear data structure; its elements are not connected in sequence. Array, queue and stack are linear data structures.

Array and the need of an index

Every element of an array is identified by an index; indexes are a set of consecutive numbers with which any element can be directly found and used. Without an index, it would not be known which element is stored where. Traversing an array means accessing each and every element of the array.

Stack: push, pop and overflow

When data is pushed in a stack, it means data is inserted. In the sketch of a stack: with Push a new element enters from the top and with Pop the top element is removed; when the stack is completely full it is in the Overflow state and nothing can be added to it.

Queue: enqueue and dequeue

In the sketch of a queue: with Enqueue a new element enters at the rear end and with Dequeue an element is removed from the front end.

Stack vs queue

StackQueue
Data is added or removed only from the topA new element enters at the rear end and the old element is removed from the front end
Works in LIFO / FILO order (last in, first out)Works in FIFO order (first in, first out)
Operations are push and popOperations are enqueue and dequeue

lessons.title: Tree and Graph Data Structures

mcqs.q: A tree is a non-linear data structure that stores data in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a hierarchical manner. The lesson defines a tree as a non-linear data structure that stores data hierarchically and shows the hierarchical relationship between elements.

mcqs.q: In a binary tree, each node can have a maximum of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: two children. The lesson states that in a binary tree each node can have a maximum of two nodes, that is, two children.

mcqs.q: A graph is made up of:
options: Nodes or vertices and edges joining them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: nodes or vertices and edges joining them. The lesson describes a graph in these terms and adds that it has no root or child.

mcqs.q: Which statement about a graph is correct?
options: It has no root or child, and each node can have many edges
It can never form a cycle
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it has no root or child, and each node can have many edges. The lesson's tree-versus-graph table gives this as a key difference, and a cycle can also be formed in a graph.

mcqs.q: Which structure can form a cycle?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: graph. The comparison table in the lesson says a tree has no cycle, while in a graph a cycle can also be formed.

mcqs.q: A tree has:
options: One root node, and every node has one parent with children
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: one root node, and every node has one parent with children. The lesson's comparison table states this for a tree, in contrast to a graph which has no root or child.

mcqs.q: What does a tree show between its elements?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a hierarchical relationship. The lesson says a tree shows the hierarchical relationship between elements, which is why its data is stored in a hierarchical manner.

mcqs.q: In the lesson's tree drawing with six nodes, the root node is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: node 1. In the drawing described in the lesson, root node 1 is at the top, its children are 2 and 3, node 2 has children 4 and 5, and node 3 has child 6.

mcqs.q: In the lesson's graph drawing with five nodes, the edges:
options: Must join a parent to a child
Can join any two nodes, and a cycle can be formed
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: edges can join any two nodes, and a cycle can be formed. The lesson's example joins nodes such as 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-5, 5-1 and 1-3, which includes a cycle.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is true for a tree but not for a graph?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it has no cycle. Both trees and graphs are non-linear and have nodes and edges, but the lesson's table says a tree has no cycle while a graph can form one.

lessons.notes_html:
Tree

A tree is a non-linear data structure that stores data in a hierarchical manner; it shows the hierarchical relationship between elements. In a binary tree, each node can have a maximum of two nodes (children).

Graph

A graph has nodes / vertices and edges joining them. It has no root or child; each node can have many edges, and a cycle can also be formed.

Tree vs graph

TreeGraph
Shows hierarchical dataNodes / vertices are joined by edges
Has one root node; every node has one parent with childrenNo root or child; each node can have many edges
No cycleA cycle can also be formed

Drawing a tree with six nodes and a graph with five nodes

(a) Tree: root node 1 at the top; its children 2 and 3; node 2's children 4 and 5; node 3's child 6 — six nodes in all, every edge from parent to child, no cycle.

(b) Graph: five nodes 1 to 5; edges can join any two nodes, for example 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 4-5, 5-1 and 1-3 — a cycle can be formed.

chapters.title: Unit 2: Basics of Programming in C++

lessons.title: Computer Programs and Programming Languages

mcqs.q: A computer program is:
options: A collection or set of instructions that a computer understands to perform tasks
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a collection or set of instructions that a computer understands to perform tasks. The lesson defines a computer program in exactly these words.

mcqs.q: The person who writes programs is called a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: programmer. The lesson says the person who writes programs is called a programmer, while a compiler is a specialized program that converts instructions into machine-readable form.

mcqs.q: Specialized programs such as a compiler convert the programmer's instructions into:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: machine-readable instructions. The lesson explains that specialized programs such as a compiler convert those instructions into machine-readable instructions.

mcqs.q: High-level languages have syntax that is:
options: Easily readable by humans, closer to human languages with English-like words
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: easily readable by humans, closer to human languages with English-like words. The lesson contrasts high-level languages with low-level languages, whose syntax is easily readable by machines and hard for humans.

mcqs.q: Low-level languages have syntax that is:
options: Easily readable by machines and hard for humans
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: easily readable by machines and hard for humans. The lesson gives this as the defining feature of low-level languages, the opposite of high-level languages.

mcqs.q: Machine language is written in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 0 and 1, that is, binary. The lesson's comparison table says machine language is at the lowest level and is written in 0 and 1.

mcqs.q: Which statement about machine language is correct?
options: It is executed directly by the computer and needs no translator
It is written in simple English
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it is executed directly by the computer and needs no translator. The lesson's table also calls machine language the first-generation language.

mcqs.q: Assembly language needs which translator to convert it into machine code?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: assembler. The lesson states that assembly language, which is one level above machine language and written in simple English, needs an assembler to convert it into machine code.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is one of the five common high-level languages named in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: PHP. The five high-level languages named in the unit are C++, Java, Python, Visual Basic and PHP, while assembly and machine language are low-level.

mcqs.q: C++ was developed as:
options: An enhancement of the C language to include the object-oriented concept
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: an enhancement of the C language to include the object-oriented concept. The lesson adds that this was done to make writing programs easier and more pleasant.

lessons.notes_html:
What is a computer program?

A computer program is a collection / set of instructions that is understood by a computer to perform tasks. The person who writes programs is called a programmer, and specialized programs such as a compiler convert those instructions into machine-readable instructions.

Low-level and high-level languages

High-level languages have syntax that is easily readable by humans — they are closer to human languages and are written in English-like words. Low-level languages have syntax that is easily readable by machines and hard for humans.

Machine language vs assembly language

Machine languageAssembly language
At the lowest level; written in 0 and 1 (binary)One level above machine language; written in simple English language, easy for humans to read, write and maintain
Executed directly by the computer; needs no translatorNeeds an assembler to convert it into machine code
First-generation languageSecond-generation language

Five common high-level languages

Languages named in the unit: C++, Java, Python, Visual Basic and PHP. C++ is a general-purpose high-level language developed as an enhancement of the C language to include the object-oriented concept and to make writing programs easier and more pleasant.

lessons.title: Translators, IDE and Program Errors

mcqs.q: A compiler translates code:
options: All at once, translating the whole program in one session and creating an executable file
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: all at once, translating the whole program in one session and creating an executable file. The lesson contrasts this with an interpreter, which translates line by line.

mcqs.q: An interpreter translates code:
options: Line by line and reports the error as soon as it is found
All at once in one session
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: line by line, and it reports the error as soon as it is found. This is the interpreter's key difference from a compiler in the lesson's comparison table.

mcqs.q: Source code is:
options: The translated form that the computer runs
A program written in any language, as the programmer writes it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a program written in any language, as the programmer writes it. The lesson defines source code this way, while the translated form that the computer runs is the object or machine code.

mcqs.q: Object code or machine code is:
options: The code typed by the programmer
The translated form that the computer runs
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the translated form that the computer runs. The lesson explains that the translator converts the source code into the target machine language, which is the object code.

mcqs.q: An IDE facilitates a programmer to do which of the following in one environment?
options: Edit source code, complete and highlight syntaxes, and debug and compile codes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: edit source code, complete and highlight syntaxes, and debug and compile codes, all in one environment. This is how the lesson describes an Integrated Development Environment.

mcqs.q: One advantage of using an IDE is that it gives:
options: Compilation, linking, loading and debugging tools in a single environment
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: compilation, linking, loading and debugging tools in a single environment. The lesson lists this first among the advantages of using an IDE.

mcqs.q: In an IDE, refactoring allows:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: comprehensive and mistake-free renaming. The lesson lists refactoring for renaming among the IDE's facilities, together with syntax highlighting and autocomplete.

mcqs.q: Which facility of an IDE improves the programming workflow by suggesting code?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: code completion. The lesson says code completion improves the programming workflow, and the IDE also gives facilities such as syntax highlighting and autocomplete.

mcqs.q: How does an IDE help ensure top-quality code?
options: It writes the whole program itself
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it automatically checks for errors to ensure top-quality code. The lesson lists automatic error checking among the advantages of using an IDE.

mcqs.q: A program with a logical error:
options: Stops immediately with a syntax message
Is caught by the compiler itself
Keeps running but gives a wrong result, so the user notices it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it keeps running but gives a wrong result, so the user notices it. The lesson says all errors detected by users are typically logical errors, while syntax errors are caught by the compiler or IDE itself.

lessons.notes_html:
Compiler and interpreter

CompilerInterpreter
Translates codes all at once — it translates the whole program in one session and creates an executable fileTranslates codes line-by-line and reports the error as soon as it is found

Source code and object code

Source code is a program written in any language, as the programmer writes it. Object / machine code is the translated form that the computer runs; the translator converts the source code into the target machine language.

Integrated Development Environment (IDE)

An IDE facilitates a programmer to edit source code, complete and highlight syntaxes, and debug and compile codes — all of these in one environment.

Advantages of using an IDE

  • An IDE gives compilation, linking, loading and debugging tools in a single environment.
  • Code completion improves the programming workflow.
  • It automatically checks for errors to ensure top-quality code.
  • Refactoring allows comprehensive and mistake-free renaming.
  • It also gives facilities such as syntax highlighting and autocomplete.

Program errors

All errors detected by users are typically logical errors: a program with a logical error keeps running but gives a wrong result, so the user notices it from the wrong result; syntax errors are caught by the compiler / IDE itself.

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types

mcqs.q: Variable names in C++ can contain:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: letters, digits and underscores. The lesson's naming rules say allowed variable names can contain letters, digits and underscores, begin with a letter or underscore, and contain no whitespaces.

mcqs.q: A variable name must begin with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a letter or an underscore. The lesson's rules state that names begin with a letter or an underscore, which is why names like _average and myVar1 are valid.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT allowed in a variable name?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: whitespaces. The lesson's naming rules say a variable name cannot contain whitespaces, cannot be a reserved word, and cannot be the same as a data type.

mcqs.q: The char data type stores a single character and takes:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 1 byte. The lesson's data type table shows char storing a single character in 1 byte of memory.

mcqs.q: The int data type stores whole numbers and takes:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 4 bytes. According to the lesson's table, int stores whole numbers in 4 bytes, the same space as float.

mcqs.q: Which data type takes the most space in memory?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: double. The lesson's table shows double storing fractional numbers in 8 bytes, which the lesson notes is the most space among the listed types.

mcqs.q: The bool data type stores:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: true or false, shown as 1 for true and 0 for false. The lesson's data type table gives this meaning for bool.

mcqs.q: In C++, strings are supported through:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the standard string class. The lesson says the C++ library supports strings through the standard string class, and a string is not a fundamental type but behaves similarly in its most basic use.

mcqs.q: A variable declaration tells the compiler:
options: The final output of the program
Where and how much storage to create for the variable, specifying a data type and a name
The value of every other variable
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: where and how much storage to create for the variable, specifying a data type and a name. The lesson gives the declaration form as: data_type variable_name;

mcqs.q: Initialization of a variable means:
options: Assigning an initial value in the declaration itself, with an equal sign
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: assigning an initial value in the declaration itself, with an equal sign. The lesson gives the form data_type variable_name = value; and notes that a value can also be assigned later.

lessons.notes_html:
Rules for naming a variable

Allowed names for declaring a variable can contain letters, digits and underscores. Names begin with a letter or an underscore, cannot contain whitespaces, cannot be one of the reserved words, and cannot be the same as a data type.

Ten meaningful and valid variable names

studentName, totalMarks, firstName, lastName, rollNo, _average, myVar1, age2, price, class10 — all begin with a letter or an underscore, contain letters, digits and underscores, have no whitespace, use no reserved word, and are all shorter than 32 characters.

Data types and memory size

Data typeStoresSpace in memory
char (character)A single character1 byte
int (integer)Whole numbers4 bytes

boolTrue or false — 0 (false) or 1 (true)—

Strings in C++

Strings are variables that store non-numerical values longer than one single character. The C++ language library supports strings through the standard string class; a string is not a fundamental type but behaves in a similar way to fundamental types in its most basic use; it can be declared without an initial value and assigned a value during execution.

Declaring and initializing a variable

A declaration tells the compiler where and how much storage to create for the variable; it specifies a data type and a name: data_type variable_name; Initialization assigns an initial value in the declaration itself, with an equal sign: data_type variable_name = value; Variables do not need to be assigned initial values; a value can also be assigned later.

lessons.notes_html:
Types of comment statements in C++

Two types: 1. Single Line Comment — with a double slash (//), for a one-line explanation; 2. Multi Line Comment — with (/* and */), for explanations over many lines. Both are ignored by the compiler, meaning they are not executed.

Escape sequences \a and \r in a program

#include<iostream> using namespace std; int main() { cout << "Beep\a"; cout << "\rStart"; return 0; }

  • \a is Alert / alarm — it causes a beep sound in the computer.
  • \r is Carriage Return — it positions the cursor at the beginning of the current line.

lessons.title: Operators in C++

mcqs.q: Arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /, %) perform:
options: Arithmetic operations or calculations on operands and give a numeric result
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: arithmetic operations or calculations on operands, giving a numeric result. The lesson contrasts these with relational operators, which test the relation between two values.

mcqs.q: Relational operators test the relation between two values and their result is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: True (1) or False (0). The lesson says relational operators are binary operators needing two operands, and their result is True (1) or False (0).

mcqs.q: The != operator belongs to the relational operators and means:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: not equal to. The lesson states that != is a relational operator meaning 'not equal to' and compares the values of two operands.

mcqs.q: Which statement about = and == is correct?
options: = is a comparison operator and == assigns a value
= is the assignment operator and == is the equal to (comparison) operator
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: = is the assignment operator and == is the equal to operator. The lesson stresses that = assigns the right-side value to the left variable, while == checks the equality of two operands.

mcqs.q: The operator used for the logical AND operation is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: &&. The lesson says the operator for logical AND is &&, and the condition will be true if both expressions are true; the logical operators are &&, || and !.

mcqs.q: Which set contains only logical operators?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: &&, || and !. The lesson lists exactly these three as the logical operators: && for AND, || for OR and ! for NOT.

mcqs.q: The += operator:
options: Adds the right operand to the left operand and assigns the result to the left operand
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it adds the right operand to the left operand and assigns the result to the left operand. The lesson defines += in exactly these words.

mcqs.q: What is the output of cout << 12 - 6 / 2; according to operator precedence?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 9. By the precedence of arithmetic operators, division comes first: 6 / 2 = 3, and then 12 - 3 = 9, as the lesson's worked example shows.

mcqs.q: In the lesson's program with int a = 27, the value printed by the postfix expression a++ is:
options: 27, because the value is printed first and then a becomes 28
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 27, because a++ is postfix: first 27 is printed, then a becomes 28. The lesson explains the outputs of a++, a, --a and a step by step in this way.

mcqs.q: In the same program, after the a++ step, the value of a becomes:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 28. The lesson explains that with postfix a++ the printed value is 27 first and then a becomes 28; later --a is prefix, so a first becomes 27 and then 27 is printed.

lessons.notes_html:
Arithmetic operators vs relational operators

Arithmetic operatorsRelational operators
(+, -, *, /, %) perform arithmetic operations / calculations on operands and give a numeric result(==, !=, >, <, >=, <=) test the relation between two values; they are binary operators, they need two operands, and their result is True (1) or False (0)

The != operator belongs to the relational operators — it means "not equal to" and compares the values of two operands. To compare two values, <= and == are both correct comparison operators; = is the assignment operator, not a comparison.

Logical operators

The operator used for the logical AND operation is && — the condition will be true if both expressions are true. The logical operators are && (AND), || (OR) and ! (NOT).

Assignment operator vs equal to operator

The assignment operator (=) assigns the value of the right-side expression to the left-side variable, for example x=10; The equal to operator (==) checks the equality of the values of two operands, for example x==y; — if the condition is true the result is true, otherwise false. The += operator adds the right operand to the left operand and assigns the result to the left operand.

Output of a program with a++, --a

Program: int a = 27; then a is displayed with a++, a, --a and a. Output: a is 27; a is now 27; a is now 28; a is now 27; a is now 27. Reason: a++ is postfix, first 27 is printed then a becomes 28; then a is printed as 28; --a is prefix, first a becomes 27 then 27 is printed; finally a is printed as 27.

Operator precedence: a worked example

cout << 12-6/2; gives 9 on the screen: by the precedence of arithmetic operators, division comes first: 6/2 = 3, then 12-3 = 9.

mcqs.q: In the lesson's assignment-operators program, a starts at 20. After a += 2, the value of a is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: 22. The program output in the lesson shows 'After += 2, a = 22', because += adds 2 to a and assigns the result back to a.

options: total / 500 x 100, because each subject is of 100 marks

Twice the sum of a and b

mcqs.q: In the lesson's error-finding program, for input 5 the correct program prints:

lessons.notes_html:
Program using all arithmetic assignment operators

#include<iostream> using namespace std; int main() { int a = 20; a += 2; cout << "After += 2, a = " << a << endl; a -= 3; cout << "After -= 3, a = " << a << endl; a *= 4; cout << "After *= 4, a = " << a << endl; a /= 4; cout << "After /= 4, a = " << a << endl; return 0; }

Output: After += 2, a = 22; After -= 3, a = 19; After *= 4, a = 76; After /= 4, a = 19.

Programs for formulas

  • Speed s = d/t: input d and t; s = d / t; display s.
  • Newton's second law F = ma: input m and a; F = m * a; display F.
  • Acceleration a = (vf - vi)/t: input vf, vi and t; a = (vf - vi) / t; display a.
  • Area of triangle a = 1/2 bh: input b and h; area = (b * h) / 2; display area.
  • Celsius to Fahrenheit F = (c * 1.8) + 32: input c; F = (c * 1.8) + 32; display F.

Every program has the same structure: #include<iostream>, using namespace std;, int main(), declaration of variables, input with cin, formula, result with cout, return 0;

Program: volume of a box

#include<iostream> using namespace std; int main() { float length, width, height, volume; cout << "Enter length, width and height"; cin >> length >> width >> height; volume = length * width * height; cout << "Volume = " << volume; return 0; }

Volume = length x width x height (the formula of Algorithm 4 of Unit 1).

Program: marksheet of five subjects

#include<iostream> using namespace std; int main() { float m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, total, percentage; cout << "Enter marks of five subjects"; cin >> m1 >> m2 >> m3 >> m4 >> m5; total = m1 + m2 + m3 + m4 + m5; percentage = total / 500 * 100; cout << "Total = " << total << " Percentage = " << percentage; return 0; }

Total 500 because each subject is of 100 marks (like the book's three-number model: Percent = Sum / 300 * 100).

Program: the expression a2 + 2ab + b2

#include<iostream> using namespace std; int main() { float a, b, result; cout << "Enter a and b"; cin >> a >> b; result = a * a + 2 * a * b + b * b; cout << "Result = " << result; return 0; }

This expression equals the square of (a + b).

Finding and removing errors from a program

Errors: 1. using namespace std is missing a semicolon (;) at the end; 2. int main() must not be followed by (;); 3. cin >> x is missing (;) at the end; 4. in a * a, a is not declared — it should be x * x. Correct program:

#include<iostream> using namespace std; int main() { int x; cout << "Enter the value of x"; cin >> x; cout << "The square of x is " << x * x; return 0; }

Output (for input 5): Enter the value of x 5; The square of x is 25.

lessons.title: Selection: if, else if and switch

mcqs.q: Using else with the if statement is:
options: Optional, because if can be used alone
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: optional, because if can be used alone. The lesson states that using else is optional with the if statement, and with else, either the if block executes or the else block.

mcqs.q: In an if-else statement:
options: Either the if block executes or the else block executes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: either the if block executes or the else block executes. The lesson explains this working of if-else, where the condition decides which single block runs.

mcqs.q: The conditions in if and loop expressions are tested using:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: relational operators. The lesson states that the if and loop expressions use relational operators to test the condition.

mcqs.q: The else if ladder is used to:
options: Test many conditions in a ladder, running the block of whichever condition is true
Match a value with case constants
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: test many conditions in a ladder, running the block of whichever condition is true. The lesson adds that otherwise the next condition is tested.

mcqs.q: The else if ladder makes a nested-if program:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: simpler and more readable. The lesson gives this benefit of the else if ladder over a nested-if program.

mcqs.q: The switch statement works by:
options: Matching the variable's value with the case constants and transferring control to the matching case
Repeating a block a fixed number of times
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: matching the variable's value with the case constants and transferring control to the matching case. The lesson adds that if none matches, control goes to default if it is present.

mcqs.q: In a switch statement, if the variable does not match any case constant, control goes to:
options: The end of the program only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: default, if it is present. The lesson explains the purpose of default in a switch in exactly this way.

mcqs.q: In a switch statement, default acts as:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: else. The lesson states that default acts as 'else' in a switch, handling the situation where no case constant matches the variable's value.

mcqs.q: 'case' and 'default' are parts of which statement?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the switch statement. The lesson lists case and default as parts of the switch statement in its matching pairs.

mcqs.q: Which data types can be used for the variable in a switch statement?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: only character and integer data type variables. The lesson adds that the value must exactly match the case constants, and relational operators like < or > cannot be used in a switch.

lessons.notes_html:
The if statement and the use of else

Using else is optional with the if statement — if can be used alone; with else, in if-else either the if block executes or the else block. The if and loop expressions use relational operators to test the condition.

The else if ladder

else if tests many conditions in a ladder — the block of whichever condition is true runs, otherwise the next condition is tested; it makes a nested-if program simpler and more readable.

The switch statement

switch matches the variable's value with the case constants and transfers control to the matching case; if none matches, to default. "case" and "default" are parts of the switch statement.

Purpose of default

In a switch, if the switch variable does not match any of the case constants, control goes to default (if it is present). Default acts as "else".

Which data types can be used in switch?

In a switch, only character and integer data type variables can be used; it matches the switch variable's value only with case constants, not with any variable, and relational operators like < or > cannot be used in it — the value must exactly match the case constants.

lessons.title: Loops: for, while and do-while

mcqs.q: The for loop is usually used when:
options: We never know how many times the block will run
We know at the start of the loop how many times the loop block will execute
The condition is tested at the end
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: when we know at the start of the loop how many times the loop block will execute. The lesson calls the for loop a counter-controlled or definite repetition loop.

mcqs.q: The for loop is called a counter-controlled or definite repetition loop, and its condition is tested:
options: At the end of the body
At the start of the loop
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: at the start of the loop. The lesson states this for the for loop, in contrast to the do-while loop whose condition is tested at the end.

mcqs.q: The three parts of a for loop expression are:
options: Initialization, condition testing, increment or decrement
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: first initialization, second condition testing, and third increment or decrement. The lesson lists the for loop expression's three parts in this order.

mcqs.q: The while loop is a pre-test loop, which means:
options: Its body always runs many times
The condition is tested at the start, so the body may not run even once
The condition is tested after the body
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the condition is tested at the start, so the body may not run even once. The lesson contrasts the while loop as a pre-test loop with the do-while as a post-test loop.

mcqs.q: The do-while loop is a post-test loop, which means:
options: The condition is tested at the start
The condition is tested at the end of the body, so its body runs at least once
It is the same as a for loop
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the condition is tested at the end of the body, so its body runs at least once. The lesson also notes that in do-while, the while(condition) part is followed by a semicolon.

mcqs.q: In a do-while loop, the while(condition) is followed by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a semicolon. The lesson points out this detail of the do-while loop: its while(condition) is followed by a semicolon.

mcqs.q: Can a while loop be used in place of a for loop?
options: Yes, by splitting the three parts: initialization before the loop, condition in while, and increment inside the body
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: yes, by splitting the three parts of the for loop. The lesson shows int i = 1; while (i <= 10) { cout << i; i++; } as the same as for (i = 1; i <= 10; i++).

mcqs.q: A loop within a loop, that is, a loop in the body of another loop, is called a:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: nested loop. The lesson defines a nested loop as a loop within a loop: if a loop exists in the body of another loop, it is called a nested loop.

mcqs.q: In converting a for loop into a while loop, the increment or decrement part is placed:
options: Inside the body of the loop
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: inside the body of the loop. The lesson explains the split: initialization before the loop, the condition in while(...), and increment or decrement inside the body.

mcqs.q: Which loop guarantees that its body runs at least once?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: the do-while loop. Because its condition is tested at the end of the body, the lesson says the do-while body runs at least once, unlike the pre-test while loop.

lessons.notes_html:
The for loop

The for loop executes a sequence of statements multiple times. It is usually used in situations where we know at the start of the loop how many times the loop block will execute; it is a counter-controlled / definite repetition loop and the condition is tested at the start of the loop. The for loop expression has three parts: first initialization, second condition testing, third increment or decrement.

while vs do-while

while loopdo-while loop
Pre-test loop: the condition is tested at the start of the loop, so the body may not run even oncePost-test loop: the condition is tested at the end of the body, so its body runs at least once; its while(condition) is followed by a semicolon

Using while in place of for

Yes. The three parts of a for loop can be split up: initialization before the loop, the condition in while(...), and increment / decrement inside the body of the loop. For example: int i = 1; while (i <= 10) { cout << i; i++; } — this is the same as for (i = 1; i <= 10; i++).

Nested loops

A loop within a loop is called a nested loop — if a loop exists in the body of another loop, then it is called a nested loop.

lessons.title: Jump Statements and Blocks of Statements

mcqs.q: Jump statements are used to:
options: Change the execution of the program from its normal sequence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: change the execution of the program from its normal sequence. The lesson says jump statements transfer control to another part of the program, terminate a loop or switch, send a value back from a function, or terminate the program.

mcqs.q: The break statement is used to:
options: Skip one iteration of a loop
Terminate a loop or switch statement
Return a value from main only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: terminate a loop or switch statement. The lesson states this use of break, and notes it is used with switch and loops.

mcqs.q: In a switch statement, break is placed:
options: At the end of each case
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: at the end of each case. The lesson points out that in a switch, break comes at the end of each case.

mcqs.q: The continue statement:
options: Skips the remaining statements of the loop body and transfers control to the top of the loop
Returns a value to the calling function
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: it skips the remaining statements of the loop body and immediately transfers control to the top of the loop. The lesson contrasts this with break, which terminates the loop or switch.

mcqs.q: The goto statement jumps control:
options: Unconditionally to a labeled statement in the same function
To the start of the program
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: unconditionally to a labeled statement in the same function. The lesson describes the goto statement in exactly these words.

mcqs.q: In a goto statement, a labeled statement is an identifier followed by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: a colon (:). The lesson says the label in a goto statement is followed by a colon character, and a labeled statement is any identifier followed by a colon.

mcqs.q: The return statement is used to:
options: Send a value to the calling function and terminate the function's execution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: send a value to the calling function and terminate the function's execution. The lesson says return terminates the execution of a function and can also return a value from the function.

mcqs.q: The exit() function is used to:
options: Terminate and close the C++ program whenever it is executed
Return from a function with a value
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: terminate and close the C++ program whenever it is executed. The lesson describes the exit() function in exactly these words.

mcqs.q: Statements are enclosed in curly braces to make a block so that they:
options: Run together as one joint part or group
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: so that they run together as one joint part or group. The lesson says more than one statement is enclosed in braces to gather them into one block, as in an if block, a loop body or a function body.

mcqs.q: Which matching pair from the lesson is correct?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: case matches with switch, because case is a part of the switch statement. The lesson's matching pairs also include break with loops and switch, and >> as the extraction or input operator.

lessons.notes_html:
Purpose of jump statements

Jump statements change the execution of the program from its normal sequence: they transfer control to another part of the program, terminate a loop or switch, send a value back from a function, or terminate the program.

break and continue

  • break is used with switch (and loops) — break terminates the loop or switch statement; in a switch, break comes at the end of each case.
  • continue takes control to the top of the loop — it causes the loop to skip the remaining statements of its body and immediately transfers control to the top.

goto, return and exit()

  • goto: jumps control unconditionally from the goto to a labeled statement in the same function; in the goto statement the label is followed by a colon (:) character — a labeled statement is any identifier followed by a colon (:).
  • return: to send a value to the calling function we use the return statement; it terminates the execution of a function and can also return a value from the function.
  • exit(): the exit() function is used to close the program — it terminates the C++ program and closes it whenever executed.

Why we make blocks of statements using braces

To gather more than one statement into one group / block, they are enclosed in curly braces, so that they run together as one joint part; for example, if there is more than one statement in an if block, the body of a loop or the body of a function, they are all enclosed in braces.

mcqs.q: In the lesson's odd-or-even program, a number is even when:
options: num % 2 == 0, that is, dividing by 2 leaves remainder 0

mcqs.q: The program that adds numbers from 1 to 20 with a for loop prints:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: Sum = 210. The lesson's program runs sum = sum + i for i from 1 to 20 with a for loop, and its output is shown as Sum = 210.

mcqs.q: In the days-in-a-month switch program, the months with 31 days are:

mcqs.q: In the same program, February (month 2) is written as having:
